newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Almaz says has PGM export licences.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Almaz says has PGM export licences.

text.p: Russian precious metals export agent Almazjuvelirexport (Almaz) said on Tuesday it had received export licences from the Foreign Trade and Economic Relations Ministry, allowing it to start long-delayed exports of platinum group metals (PGMs).
"We received the licence (from the Foreign Trade and Economic Relations Ministry) in the last few days," said Sergei Gorny, deputy director of Almaz.
"First there is a government decree which sets out the quotas, and then based on that decree the ministry hands out the licences," he said.
The government decree on export quotas was signed in late-April or early-May.

But Yuri Boikin, deputy head of the ministry's foreign economic activities department, said last week that Almaz could deliver platinum and palladium abroad almost as soon as they wished after getting the quota.
"They can do it (export) whenever they want," Boikin had said. "On the second day after getting the quota they can get a general licence."

Vladimir Rybkin, head of the Finance Ministry's precious metals and stones department, said on Tuesday that the export licence and the export quota decree were not directly linked, and that the licence was necessary for exports.
Almaz's Gorny said there would be no further delays in exporting platinum and palladium to overseas clients, after six-month delays in Russian exports sent prices for both metals to record highs.
Russia supplies 20 percent of the world's platinum and 60 percent of its palladium.

It held talks with clients in Japan, the world's largest consumer of both metals, earlier this month, and Gorny said the talks had been satisfactory and that Almaz would carry out its contractual obligations.
